_batch: The plating batch, e.g. fall2026_batch1_iPSC_M1. With chip, plate_date, div and well it names the recording in the store.
_phase: all: one recording. Or split a conditioning session into recordings that are each read back before the next: baseline, encode_1..encode_<encode_cycles>, retrieval. The phase is appended to the file name. phase_lead_min is the quiet at the start of each encode recording.
description: associative conditioning: US+CS paired and NS alone; every region probed alone before, after, and after rests
_rec_electrodes: Filled in by `select`. Every electrode to record; the regions' patches plus a spread over the rest.
_regions: Centres in um, x along the long axis (0-3832), y along the short (0-2082). Filled in by `select`; then keep them fixed for the culture.
_amplitudes_mv: Per role, mV PER PHASE; peak to peak is twice this. Ronchi et al. 2019 characterised 40-240 mV peak to peak (20-120 per phase) on these arrays, so the ladder stays in that range and max_amplitude_mv refuses anything above 150 per phase unless raised deliberately.
_amplitudes_source: Where amplitudes_mv came from. 'default' means nobody calibrated, and connectivity and conditioning runs refuse to start on it: run calibration, paste the two lines its report prints (amplitudes_mv and amplitudes_source) here.
_stim_site: focal: an inner x inner driven block on drive_dac, ringed by return electrodes on return_dac carrying the inverted pulse, which confines the field (Ronchi et al. 2019). The ring is laid out around the block itself, so it is centred on it whatever the spacing. The default drives four electrodes 122.5 um apart with two return electrodes at opposite corners, 220 um from the block's centre. Why two and not four: the chip's 32 stimulation units each serve an area of the array, and an area exposes only about seven of them (measured on a MaxOne), so a site of eight electrodes cannot be connected while one of six can. return_points 'corners' is the four-corner ring, if a chip allows it. Widen a site with inner_gap, not inner: a focal site costs inner^2 + return points units of the 32, and a 3x3 focal site will not fit. grid: {shape, size, gap}, one DAC per role from region_dacs, no return ring.
_stim_phase_us: Biphasic, charge balanced. 100 us per phase is enough and keeps the artifact short; anodic-first was the more effective order in voltage mode (Ronchi et al. 2019).
_pulse_hz: A presentation is t_stim (training) or t_probe (probe) seconds of pulse events at pulse_hz. pulses_per_burst 1 is a single pulse per event; 11 at burst_hz 20 is a Jimbo-style tetanus.
_mode: conditioning, or calibration: single pulses at every calibration amplitude and polarity, per region.
_pre_min: Minutes. probe_iti, encode_iti, encode_cycle_rest, calibration_iti, t_stim, t_probe are seconds; dt_cs_us and the windows are ms.
_probe_roles: Each probe is t_probe seconds at pulse_hz (20 pulses); probe_reps of each role per block gives 60 probe pulses per role to estimate a response probability from. Retrieval probes all three roles so a US-alone change in excitability is not read as learning. Every probe is also a little extinction, so keep probe pulses small next to the paired ones.
_encode_pattern: encode_cycles cycles of encode_pattern (encode_iti apart) then encode_cycle_rest seconds of nothing. The default is four cycles of PAIR, NS, PAIR, NS: 4.5 min trains 5.5 min apart, 4 min of rest between cycles, 99 min and 712 paired pulses, and NS receives exactly as much stimulation as CS but never together with US, which is what rules out 'any region driven for an hour grows a path to US'. The rate is the part not to raise: a pulse evokes a network response lasting a few hundred ms and the response depresses if the next comes too soon, so sustained pairing in vitro sits at 0.2-1 Hz for tens of minutes (Shahaf & Marom 2001; le Feber 2010, 2015). Trade pairing against length with encode_cycles, and pairing against the control with the pattern (PAIR, PAIR, NS gives half again as many paired pulses and NS half the dose). encode_iti must cover t_stim; probe_iti must cover t_probe plus the response windows.
_encode_probe_roles: Between cycles, after the rest, each of these roles is probed alone encode_probe_reps times, probe_iti apart: a checkpoint on the way, so the result is a curve of how fast the association forms and not only where it ended up. CS alone is the measurement and NS alone its control; adding US costs another probe per checkpoint for an excitability check the baseline and retrieval blocks already make. Empty for none. A checkpoint is an unpaired CS presentation in the middle of acquisition, which is what extinction is, so it is kept short: encode_probe_sec 30 s is 10 pulses a probe, 60 across the whole encode block against 712 paired ones. The report counts per pulse, so these stay comparable with the full probe blocks that anchor the curve.
_raw_traces: spikes are always kept, for every routed channel. raw_traces adds raw voltage: none (spikes only, ~1 MB a minute; the readout needs nothing more), regions (the three regions' recording and stimulation electrodes, enough to see the stimulation artifact), all (every channel: ~4 kB per channel-second on a MaxTwo, twice on a MaxOne, tens of GB for a four-hour run).
_pulse_window_ms: Counted after every pulse of a presentation and summed: the readout. response_windows_ms is optional; without it the windows are base/during/after sized by t_probe.
